newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes slightly higher, term talks in focus.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes slightly higher, term talks in focus.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were marginally higher on Friday as term crude talks kept centre stage.
Paper Tapis was slightly firmer on the day with December quoted in late afternoon dealings at $23.05/$23.15, up around 15 cents on the day.
November was notionally assessed at a 45-cent backwardation to December, although talk was quiet with most focus now on December.
December Tapis traded at $23.15 and $23.20 for 50,000 barrels a piece.
Dubai spreads were mostly unchanged along with a steady Brent/Dubai.
However, traders said Dubai was under pressure and its spreads could come in further as players sell the Dubai/gas oil crack.

Singapore prompt gas oil traded at a five-year high of $30.60 per barrel on Friday, defying the gas oil slump in Europe and North America and sparking players to lock in a Q1 1997 gas oil/Dubai crack at $9.00 per barrel.
There was little physical talk on crude with most focus still on term talks.
Stasco's round of talks are expected to be concluded next week, with the major talking around a premium of 10 to 15 cents over MPM compared with plus eight in 1996.
The December Kutubu deal said traded earlier this week was confirmed at Tapis quotes plus 27 cents. It took place between a European major and a U.S. major.
LG Caltex confirmed it had agreed to take on term 30,000 barrels per day of Alaskan North Slope crude, effective December 20. Its new 220,000 barrels per day CDU comes on stream in November.
